items.subtitle: Import Preferences
items.contents:
Import Preferences

Import Pref... loads an editor preference JSON file previously downloaded from Node2D. Stored editor settings and saved shortcut choices are restored from the file, so the editor changes to match the imported preferences.

The import can also restore stored preference keys contained in the exported preference data, allowing newer preference values to be carried between editor versions.

items.subtitle: Multiselection Unified Editing
items.contents:
Multiselection Unified Editing

Multiselection Unified Editing is a Bool editor setting and is True by default.

When True, multiple selected Nodes behave like one object for Move, Scale, and Rotate. Scaling changes the group as a whole while preserving each Node's relative position and size. Rotating turns the group around its combined center.

The selection gets one large yellow outline covering the whole group.

When False, each selected Node gets its own yellow outline. Scale changes each Node individually, and Rotate changes each Node's own angle without orbiting its position around the group center.

items.subtitle: Create New Missing Component
items.contents:
Create New Missing Component

Default: False.

When enabled, a multi-selection edit can create the edited Component on Nodes that do not currently have it. This is useful when you want a group of Nodes to end up with the same Component property even if some Nodes started without that Component.

items.subtitle: Automatic offline mode
items.contents:
Automatic offline mode

Node2D caches its editor files in your browser whenever you visit it while online.

  • Online: loads the newest editor files and refreshes the browser cache.
  • Offline: opens from the most recently cached editor copy.
  • Online again: requests the newest version and updates the cache when the newer files are available.

The editor cache is separate from Local NDC project storage.

items.contents:
Offline message

items.subtitle: PWA installation
items.contents:
PWA

The editor itself can be used as a Progressive Web App when the browser supports installation. This is separate from exporting a game as a PWA: the editor can also have its own installable/offline behavior.

items.subtitle: Landscape PWA preference
items.contents:
Landscape PWA preference

The Node2D Game Engine PWA manifest requests landscape orientation. On browsers and installed-app environments that support the manifest orientation setting, the installed app prefers to open in landscape.

items.subtitle: Components
items.contents:
Components

Node — object identity. Script — visual script graph. Transform — position, scale, rotation. Text — displayed text. Sprite — images and animated presentation. Animation Sprite — collections of sprite frames. Physics — physical movement. Collider — collision shape. Progress Bar — value meter. Joystick — touch control.

Boolean · Interval · Timeout · isCollidedWith

onConnectionChange

onConnectionChange is an Event ScriptNode with a Connection selector containing Online and Offline. It sends out when the browser changes network connection state while the game is running.

items.contents:
Editor Snap

Default Move / Scale Snap: 1. Default Rotate Snap: 0° (Off). Both settings can be changed in Editor Settings and are saved on your device.

items.subtitle: Audio playback inputs
items.contents:
Audio playback inputs

playAudio uses src, volume, start, duration, loop, fadein, and fadeout. Volume is a 0–100 value. Frequently played short sounds are decoded and cached so later calls can be scheduled with very little playback overhead.

Microphone ScriptNodes

Multi-selection editing

items.subtitle: A variable name was rejected
items.contents:
Variable name rejected

Choose a name that is not already used in a conflicting scope. The editor keeps the last valid name and shows the field with red error styling when a conflict is detected.

items.subtitle: An asset was rejected
items.contents:
Asset rejected

Check that the file is a supported image or audio type for the drop/import area you are using. Unsupported file types are intentionally rejected.

items.subtitle: The game view does not fit the screen
items.contents:
Game view fitting

Check Game Settings → Screen Type. Windowboxing keeps the 16:9 shape, Stretch fills the screen, Crop fills the screen while cutting edges, and Smart Camera changes the visible camera area.

items.subtitle: A MIDI file is still loading
items.contents:
MIDI loading

Large MIDI files can take time to process. Watch the loading percentage shown by the MIDI Editor instead of assuming the editor is frozen.

items.subtitle: The editor is too narrow
items.contents:
Editor too narrow

Rotate the device or expand the window when the editor displays the small-screen warning. Editing is intentionally blocked while the screen is too narrow.

items.subtitle: Objects move by tiny decimal amounts
items.contents:
Objects move by tiny decimal amounts

Check Editor Settings → Move / Scale Snap. A value such as 0.1 makes the position and scale use tenth-unit steps while the gizmo is dragged.

Snapping is applied to the Move gizmo center/axes and to the Scale gizmo handles. Rotation has its own separate snap setting.

items.subtitle: Scale corner does not keep the ratio
items.contents:
Scale corner behavior

Use a corner handle when you want a proportional resize. Corner handles preserve the starting width-to-height ratio. Use a side handle when you intentionally want to change only width or only height.

items.subtitle: ScriptNode placement
items.contents:
ScriptNode placement

When adding a ScriptNode from the library, Node2D places it at the center of the currently visible Script canvas, taking the current pan and zoom into account. Dragging a ScriptNode into the canvas places it at the actual drop location.

items.subtitle: Mixed-value control does not commit
items.contents:
Multi-selection value will not commit

Press Enter or click/focus outside the control. Changing selection also forces the active edit to commit before the inspector is rebuilt. If values differ, first click <> to activate the normal field; the field starts from the first selected Node and then applies the committed value to the current selection.
